Chapter Eight: Creativity as Survival
You know, there’s a certain magic in making something out of nothing. For a lot of us, creativity isn’t just a hobby or something we do for work—it’s how we get by. It’s how we make sense of the world, and sometimes, it’s how we find little pockets of joy in the middle of all the chaos.
But let’s be honest—the creative journey is almost never easy. It’s full of doubt, of starting over, of that nagging voice whispering, “Is anything I make ever really good enough?”
Think about a writer, for example. For her, creativity became both a safe haven and, at times, a real struggle. There were days when words just flowed, when ideas caught fire and turned into something real. But then came those long stretches of frustration—staring at blank pages, facing rejected pitches, and feeling like everyone else was more talented, more original, more deserving. The urge to quit? It was always there, just hiding in the background.
And yet, every time, she came back to the work. Sometimes out of pure stubbornness, other times because she still had hope—or just because, honestly, there was no other way to make sense of things. Most people never see the hours spent alone, or the drafts that never make it past her desk. They don’t see those quiet little victories—like finishing something that once felt impossible.
You start to realize, after a while, that creativity isn’t about waiting for some flash of inspiration. It’s about showing up, day after day, even when it seems pointless. It’s about trusting that the process itself matters—that simply making something, no matter how small, is its own kind of reward.
And here’s something you might not expect: the best ideas? They don’t usually arrive in a burst of brilliance. Most of them show up in the slow, steady work of trying, failing, and trying again.
So if you’re on your own creative path—just remember, you’re not alone. The struggle is part of the magic. And every time you choose to keep going, you’re already winning.
